**Conversation Overview**

The person is building a scalable agency model called The Luxora Collective, targeting med spa owners. They are working on creating a 90-Day Client Action Checklist Excel workbook that aligns precisely with their 90-Day Transformation Roadmap and client onboarding process. Key team members mentioned include Jacques (handles Meta ad configuration and CRM/GHL technical builds) and Aanchal (helps coordinate client outreach). The person emphasized repeatedly that this is a done-with-you program, not done-for-you, with biweekly 30-minute check-ins and Slack support between calls — intentionally designed so Luxora is not handholding every client daily, preserving a scalable agency model.

Claude built and iteratively refined a multi-tab Excel workbook across five versions, using Python and openpyxl with Luxora's brand palette (champagne, deep bronze, ivory). The workbook contains eight tabs: Start Here, Pre-Kickoff Onboarding, Days 1-30 Foundation, Days 31-60 Optimization, Days 61-90 Celebration, Post-Event Success Call, KPI Dashboard, and Playbook Delivery Log. Several important structural corrections were made throughout: the Revenue Leak Audit was removed entirely (it happens on the sales call pre-signup, not during the 90 days); the Market Blueprint was repositioned as a Luxora deliverable arriving 72 hours post-kickoff, informing the retargeting offer for existing clients; retargeting ads launch in Weeks 2-4 targeting warm audiences, while the Grand Slam offer ads are built collaboratively in Month 2 after market data reveals what resonates, then launched to cold audiences in Week 8. The Partnership playbook was reframed as directional and ongoing rather than a completion deliverable, with 1-2 partners ideally folded into the Celebration Event. The Reputation Engine playbook is client-owned and implemented by the client, with Luxora installing only the AI automation piece inside GHL.

The person clarified the long-term business model: the 90-day program is designed to transform how med spa owners think about lifetime value and membership, and the goal is for clients to continue as monthly retainer partners afterward for ongoing ad management, CRM and AI support, and monthly strategy check-ins. The ownership language across all tabs was reframed from "Owner/Tech Team" to "You/Your Team/You + Luxora/Luxora/Luxora delivers" to reflect done-with-you reality. The Start Here tab was updated to include an explicit "How This Partnership Works" section splitting Luxora's scope from the client's scope. Two recurring open items noted across versions: Slack response time expectations are not yet bounded in the document, and Phase 1 still delivers four playbooks simultaneously in Weeks 2-3, which may be unrealistic for solo spa owners.

   246	- [ ] **Far-right columns**: FY data often in columns 50+

   249	- [ ] **Wrong references**: Verify all cell references point to intended cells (#REF!)

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side

wb = Workbook()

# ============================================================
# SHEET 1: Overview & Instructions
# ============================================================

ws.title = "Start Here"

ws.column_dimensions['A'].width = 4
ws.column_dimensions['B'].width = 95

ws['B2'] = "The Luxora Growth Engine"
ws['B2'].font = title_font
ws['B3'] = "90-Day Client Action Checklist"
ws['B3'].font = Font(name="Arial", size=14, bold=True, color=DEEP_BRONZE)
ws['B4'] = "Your complete implementation guide, organized exactly the way we'll work through it together."
ws['B4'].font = subtitle_font

ws['B6'] = "How to use this workbook"

ws['B7'] = "Each tab represents a phase of your 90 days. Work through them in order. Check off each item as you complete it."

ws['B7'].alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="top")
ws.row_dimensions[7].height = 32

instructions = [
    ("1. Pre-Kickoff Onboarding (Days 1-7)", "Complete onboarding BEFORE your Strategy Kickoff Call. This is how we hit the ground running."),
    ("2. Days 1-30: Foundation & Systems Build", "Biweekly Calls #1 and #2. Receive your Sales, Laser ROI, Membership, and Package playbooks."),

]

row += 1

row += 1

# ============================================================
# Helper to build a checklist sheet
# ============================================================
def build_checklist_sheet(ws, header_title, header_subtitle, call_label, call_agenda, items, phase_color, phase_accent):
    """
    items = list of dicts with keys:
      category, action, owner, week, notes
    """
    ws.column_dimensions['A'].width = 3
    ws.column_dimensions['B'].width = 6    # Done checkbox
    ws.column_dimensions['C'].width = 22   # Category
    ws.column_dimensions['D'].width = 62   # Action
    ws.column_dimensions['E'].width = 18   # Owner
    ws.column_dimensions['F'].width = 12   # Week
    ws.column_dimensions['G'].width = 35   # Notes

    # Title
    ws.merge_cells('B2:G2')
    ws['B2'] = header_title
    ws['B2'].font = Font(name="Arial", size=20, bold=True, color=CHARCOAL)
    ws['B2'].alignment = Alignment(vertical="center")
    ws.row_dimensions[2].height = 30

    ws.merge_cells('B3:G3')
    ws['B3'] = header_subtitle
    ws['B3'].font = Font(name="Arial", size=11, italic=True, color=WARM_GRAY)
    ws['B3'].alignment = Alignment(vertical="center")
    ws.row_dimensions[3].height = 20

    # Call callout box
    ws.merge_cells('B5:G5')
    ws['B5'] = call_label
    ws['B5'].font = Font(name="Arial", size=12, bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
    ws['B5'].fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=phase_accent)
    ws['B5'].alignment = Alignment(vertical="center", indent=1)
    ws.row_dimensions[5].height = 24

    call_row = 6
    for agenda_item in call_agenda:
        ws.merge_cells(f'B{call_row}:G{call_row}')
        ws[f'B{call_row}'] = f"   • {agenda_item}"
        ws[f'B{call_row}'].font = Font(name="Arial", size=11, color=CHARCOAL)
        ws[f'B{call_row}'].fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=phase_color)
        ws[f'B{call_row}'].alignment = Alignment(vertical="center", indent=1)
        ws.row_dimensions[call_row].height = 18
        call_row += 1

    # Table header
    header_row = call_row + 1
    headers = ["Done", "Category", "Action Item", "Owner", "Week", "Notes"]
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell = ws.cell(row=header_row, column=i+2, value=h)
        cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=11, bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
        cell.fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=DEEP_BRONZE)
        cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")
        cell.border = Border(
            left=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
            right=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
            top=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
            bottom=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
        )
    ws.row_dimensions[header_row].height = 26

    # Data rows
    current_category = None
    r = header_row + 1
    for item in items:
        # Category row (group header) if new category
        if item["category"] != current_category:
            ws.merge_cells(f'C{r}:G{r}')
            ws.cell(row=r, column=2).fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=phase_color)
            cat_cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=3, value=item["category"])
            cat_cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=11, bold=True, color=DEEP_BRONZE)
            cat_cell.fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=phase_color)
            cat_cell.alignment = Alignment(vertical="center", indent=1)
            ws.row_dimensions[r].height = 22
            current_category = item["category"]
            r += 1

        # The actual action row
        ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value="☐").font = Font(name="Arial", size=14, color=DEEP_BRONZE)
        ws.cell(row=r, column=2).alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")

        ws.cell(row=r, column=3, value="").font = Font(name="Arial", size=10, color=WARM_GRAY)
        ws.cell(row=r, column=3).alignment = Alignment(vertical="center", indent=1)

        action_cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=4, value=item["action"])
        action_cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=11, color=CHARCOAL)
        action_cell.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="center", indent=1)

        owner_cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=5, value=item["owner"])
        owner_cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=10, color=WARM_GRAY)
        owner_cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")

        week_cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=6, value=item["week"])
        week_cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=10, color=WARM_GRAY)
        week_cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")

        notes_cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=7, value=item.get("notes", ""))
        notes_cell.font = Font(name="Arial", size=10, color=WARM_GRAY)
        notes_cell.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="center", indent=1)

        for col in range(2, 8):
            ws.cell(row=r, column=col).border = Border(
                left=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
                right=Side(style="thin", color=BORDER_GRAY),
                top=Side(style="hair", color=BORDER_GRAY),
                bottom=Side(style="hair", color=BORDER_GRAY),
            )
        # Alternate row shading lightly
        if (r - header_row) % 2 == 0:
            for col in range(2, 8):
                ws.cell(row=r, column=col).fill = PatternFill("solid", start_color=IVORY)

        # Row height based on action text length
        action_len = len(item["action"]) + len(item.get("notes", ""))
        ws.row_dimensions[r].height = max(30, min(60, 18 + action_len // 8))

        r += 1

**Two fixes made:**

1. **Retargeting offer lock is now an explicit Biweekly Call #1 action row.** Reads "LOCK THE RETARGETING OFFER on Biweekly Call #1. Agree on the specific offer, price, bonuses, and expiration." Owned by Owner + Luxora, Week 2. No longer buried in Blueprint review notes.

2. **Month 2 rebalanced.** Partnership delivers on Call #3 (outreach takes weeks to warm). Reputation Engine shifts to Call #4 at Week 8, with install running Weeks 8-10. Month 2 cadence is now: Weeks 5-7 focus on Grand Slam build (Luxora + Tech + Owner) and Partnership outreach (Owner). Week 8 launches Grand Slam ads and delivers Reputation. Weeks 8-10 install the review engine. No longer stacking four playbook workstreams on top of the Grand Slam build.

**Two weakest parts of this v4:**

1. **"Lifetime Value Sales Playbook" still delivers alongside three other playbooks on Call #1 Week 2.** Phase 1 loads four playbooks in one week: Sales, Laser ROI, Membership, Package Architecture. That's the original Quiz Deliverables PDF structure, but the same overload logic that pushed Reputation to Week 8 applies here. The Sales Playbook alone is the biggest read-and-train in the set. Worth considering whether Laser ROI and Package Architecture slide to Call #2 so Weeks 2-3 can focus on Sales and Membership.

2. **No explicit owner-level triage when things slip.** Every row assumes the checklist gets done on time. If a client misses Week 2 retargeting launch by 10 days, the downstream Grand Slam data-review on Call #3 has less signal. A simple "If you're behind, here's what to deprioritize" callout on each phase tab would make this a real operations tool instead of an aspirational one.

**What changed in this build:**

1. **Start Here tab now has a "How This Partnership Works" callout** that names it explicitly as a done-with-you program with biweekly 30-min check-ins and Slack support between calls (no daily handholding). Split into two scope sections:
   - **What Luxora handles:** Market Blueprint, all ad creation/management/scaling, CRM + AI + landing pages, all playbook materials, biweekly 30-min calls and Slack support
   - **What you and your team handle:** playbook reading, team training, sales/membership/package implementation, front-desk review asks, event execution, KPI tracking

2. **Ownership column reframed across all 5 phase tabs** from "Owner" / "Tech Team" to **"You"**, **"Your Team"**, **"You + Luxora"**, **"Luxora"**, and **"Luxora delivers"** (for playbook drop-offs). This reflects reality: the client does the spa-side work, Luxora does the backend and strategy.

3. **Biweekly call labels now say "30 min"** in every category header so the time expectation is baked in: "Biweekly Call #1 (Week 2, 30 min)", etc.

4. **Slack support references added** in the Sales Playbook, Membership, and Event rows so the client knows where to direct questions between calls instead of pinging you daily.

5. **Post-Event Success Call repositioned toward the monthly retainer path.** New "Long-Term Partnership Decision" section explicitly covers continued ad management, CRM and AI support, and monthly strategy check-ins. Positions the monthly retainer as the natural continuation.

**File is built, verified zero formula errors, but I hit tool limit before moving to outputs and presenting.** Say "present it" or "continue" on your next turn and I'll move the v5 to outputs and share it. File lives at `/home/claude/luxora/Luxora_90Day_Client_Action_Checklist_v2.xlsx`.

**Two weakest parts:**

1. **The scope callout on Start Here lists Slack but doesn't state the response time or what qualifies as a Slack question vs a "bring it to the next call" question.** Without that line, clients will still ping you expecting same-day replies. Worth adding something like "Slack responses within 24 hours business days. Strategic questions go on the biweekly call agenda."

2. **Phase 1 still has the client reading four playbooks in Weeks 2-3 (Sales, Laser ROI, Membership, Package).** The ownership reframe fixed the "who does it" problem but not the "when is it realistic" problem. Reading 100+ pages plus running team training plus rolling out memberships inside 14 days is still a lot. Worth considering staggered delivery: Sales + Membership on Call #1, then Laser ROI + Package on Call #2 two weeks later.

**What's in this version:**

The Start Here tab now opens with the "How This Partnership Works" callout that clearly splits Luxora's scope from the client's scope, and names the biweekly 30-minute structure with Slack between calls. **Two weakest parts still standing:**

1. **Slack expectations are named but not bounded.** "Slack support between calls" is in the scope callout, but there's no response-time expectation or guardrail on what qualifies as a Slack question vs. a "bring it to the next call" question. Strategy questions go on the biweekly call agenda."

2. **Phase 1 still asks the client to read four playbooks in Weeks 2-3.** The ownership reframe fixed "who does it" but not "is this humanly realistic." Reading Sales, Laser ROI, Membership, and Package playbooks plus running team training plus launching membership inside 14 days is a lot. Staggering delivery would help: Sales + Membership on Call #1, then Laser ROI + Package on Call #2 two weeks later.
